entry.title: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS. Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
entry.summary:
Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce. We present an empirical assessment of PQC deployment across seven critical protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP) using 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #post-quantum

entry.title: Beyond-Birthday-Bound Security with HCTR2: Cascaded Construction and Tweak-based Key Derivation
entry.summary:
The block cipher (BC) mode for realizing a variable-input-length strong tweakable pseudorandom permutation (VIL-STPRP), also known as the accordion mode, is a rapidly growing research field driven by NIST's standardization project, which considers AES as a primitive. Widely used VIL-STPRP modes, such as HCTR2, have birthday-bound security and provide only 64-bit security with AES. To provide higher security, NIST is considering two directions: to develop new modes with beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security and to use Rijndael-256-256 with HCTR2.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: RoKoko: Lattice-based Succinct Arguments, a Committed Refinement
entry.summary:
We present RoKoko, a new lattice-based succinct argument system that achieves a linear-time prover alongside polylogarithmic communication and verifier complexity. Asymptotically, our construction improves upon RoK and Roll (ASIACRYPT 2025), the first post-quantum SNARK with $\tilde{O}(\lambda)$ proof size, by a multiplicative factor of $\Theta(\log \lambda)$. Practically, our system yields proofs of roughly $200$KB, while outperforming the state-of-the-art polynomial commitment scheme Greyhound (CRYPTO 2024) with a $100\times$ faster verification time, similar prover time, and competitive proof size.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: AirBB: Lightweight Threshold Anonymous Credentials without Random Oracles from BB Signatures
entry.summary:
Anonymous credentials are a well-studied cryptographic primitive enabling users to prove statements about their identity and selectively present personal information in an unlinkable manner. The issuer, however, is often a single point of failure. Threshold issuance addresses this by distributing the issuer across several parties such that a quorum of them must cooperate to issue credentials.

entry.title: Sonata: Certifying Canonical Openings in High-Arity Lattice Folding. Folding lets a prover certify a computation incrementally by combining committed instances into an accumulator.
entry.summary:
Folding lets a prover certify a computation incrementally by combining committed instances into an accumulator. In lattice-based folding, a linear combination of field values can change their canonical digit representations. Re-encoding the result gives the prover a short opening.

entry.title: Optimality and Efficiency of Higher-Order Rank-Based Side-Channel Attacks against Inner Product Masking Schemes
entry.summary:
Higher-Order Spearman Coefficient Analysis (HO-SPA) is of particular interest in non-profiling Side-Channel Attacks (SCA) due to its effectiveness against monotonic nonlinear leakage. However, the optimal form, effective order combinations, and performance of HO-SPA (or its variants) remain underexplored. This work systematically revisits HO-SPA in the presence of Boolean Masking (BM) and Inner Product Masking (IPM).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Non-Interactive Threshold Mercurial Signatures with Applications to Threshold DAC
entry.summary:
In a mercurial signature, a signer signs a representative $m$ of an equivalence class of messages on behalf of a representative $\mathsf{pk}$ of an equivalence class of public keys, receiving the signature $\sigma$. One can then transform $\sigma$ into a signature $\sigma'$ on an equivalent (to $m$) message $m'$ under an equivalent (to $\mathsf{pk}$) public key $\mathsf{pk}'$. Mercurial signatures are helpful in constructing delegatable anonymous credentials (DACs): their privacy properties enable straightforward randomization of a credential chain, hiding the identity of each signer while preserving the authenticity of the overall credential.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust
